mainTopic: Scroll layout and margins, the proper size of a ספר תורה, and where the ספר תורה was kept in or beside the ארון
overview: The גמרא first explains the line 'if he wants to cut, he may cut': the books are laid out so that the scroll can be cut neatly between them. It then sets this ברייתא against another one that seems to give the same blank margin at both ends of a scroll. רב נחמן בר יצחק says each end gets the amount it needs. רב אשי says the second ברייתא is about a ספר תורה, which has a pole at each end. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a ספר תורה's height should equal its rolled-up circumference, and רבי gives six טפחים for a scroll on גויל. Stories follow about how rarely scribes achieved this, and about two reports of 'four hundred' that are read in a smaller way. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the measurements of משה's ארון. רבי מאיר places the ספר תורה inside it, and רבי יהודה places the ספר תורה on the פלשתים' chest beside it. The ברייתא's explanation of 'אין בארון רק' for רבי יהודה continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The last line of the scroll-layout teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the closing clause of the ברייתא: if he wants to cut the scroll, he may cut it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he comes to cut, he cuts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the ברייתא about laying out a scroll. This sets up a question about what the line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described where each book should end and the next should begin. Now it suddenly mentions cutting the scroll. It is not clear how cutting connects to the layout rules, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: to cut (here, to cut the scroll into separate pieces)

phrases.english: And if he wishes to cut, he may cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם בָּא לַחְתּוֹךְ חוֹתֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד by quoting its final clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scroll holding several books may be cut apart.

steps.title: What does this line mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is trying to say with the cutting clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the cutting line means and how it fits with the layout rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line reads like a separate permission that has nothing to do with the layout instructions before it. The גמרא wants to know why it appears here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (a request to explain unclear wording)

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the clause quoted in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the cutting clause connects to the layout rules of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The layout is arranged so that cutting is possible
steps.stepSummary: The cutting clause explains the reason for the layout: each book starts at the top of a new column so the scroll can be cut neatly.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: so that if he wants to cut, he can cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line gives the reason for the layout rule. The books are set up this way so that the scroll can be cut apart later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading the line as 'so that if' instead of 'and if', the cutting becomes the purpose of the layout. When a new book starts at the top of a fresh column, the scroll can be cut between books, and no piece will begin with blank space.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a corrected reading)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
so that if he wishes to cut, he may cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר שֶׁאִם בָּא לַחְתּוֹךְ חוֹתֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause gives the purpose of the layout: it allows the scroll to be cut neatly between books.
steps.whatToRemember: 'וְאִם' is read as 'שֶׁאִם'. The layout rules exist so that the scroll can be cut apart later.

steps.title: Another teaching about blank space at both ends
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא: leave enough parchment at the beginning and end of a scroll for rolling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with this: at the beginning of a scroll and at its end, leave enough to roll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to compare with the first one. This sets up a contradiction that will become clear in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא gave two different measures: enough to roll around the pole at the beginning, and enough to roll around the whole scroll at the end. This new ברייתא seems to give one measure for both ends.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it with (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
At the beginning of a scroll and its end, enough to wind.
phrases.notes: Enough blank parchment to wrap around.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי תְּחִלַּת סֵפֶר וְסוֹפוֹ כְּדֵי לָגוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in an outside ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's two different measures for the start and the end of the scroll.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single measure for both ends cannot match two different measures.

steps.title: Either way, the two teachings clash
steps.stepSummary: Whichever measure 'enough to roll' means, it contradicts one half of the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Enough to roll around what? If it means around the pole, the 'around the whole scroll' rule is a problem. If it means around the whole scroll, the 'around the pole' rule is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two ברייתות clash no matter how we read the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא uses one measure for both ends. If that measure is 'around the pole', it contradicts the first ברייתא's rule for the end of the scroll. If it is 'around the whole scroll', it contradicts the first ברייתא's rule for the beginning.

keyTerms.meaning: the pole the scroll is attached to
the circumference, meaning around the whole rolled scroll
it is difficult (there is a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: Here עַמּוּד means the wooden pole, not a column of writing and not a page of גמרא.

phrases.english: Enough to wind around what?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּדֵי לָגוֹל עַמּוּד – קַשְׁיָא הֶקֵּף;
phrases.english: If it means enough to wind around the pole, the circumference is difficult;
phrases.notes: That would clash with the first ברייתא, which says 'around the whole scroll' at the end.

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּדֵי לָגוֹל הֶקֵּף – קַשְׁיָא עַמּוּד!
phrases.english: if it means enough to wind around the circumference, the pole is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי לָגוֹל מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the contradiction set up in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Fitting the second ברייתא's single measure with the first ברייתא's two measures.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: each possible reading contradicts one of the two measures.

steps.title: Each end gets its own measure
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the second ברייתא speaks about each end separately, giving each the amount it needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it teaches each side separately.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that 'enough to roll' means a different amount for each end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not set one measure. It means 'enough for what that end needs': around the pole at the beginning, around the whole scroll at the end. So the second ברייתא says the same thing as the first.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches each side separately (one phrase covering two cases)
an אמורא who answers the contradiction

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It teaches each side separately.
phrases.notes: So 'enough to roll' means around the pole at the start and around the whole scroll at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לִצְדָדִין קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: one general phrase applies differently to two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'enough to roll' set the same measure for both ends.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means each end gets the amount it needs, which matches the first ברייתא.

steps.title: The second teaching is about a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: the second ברייתא really does give one measure for both ends, but it is talking about a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: when that ברייתא was taught, it was about a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer: the two ברייתות are about different kinds of scrolls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא is about other scrolls, which have a pole only at the beginning. The second ברייתא is about a ספר תורה. If a ספר תורה has a pole at each end, both ends need the same measure, and the next step proves that it does.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When that one is taught, it refers to a Torah scroll.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the second ברייתא, the one with the same measure at both ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the contradiction of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: each ברייתא is about a different kind of scroll.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are about the same kind of scroll.
steps.terutzMaskana: The single-measure ברייתא is about a ספר תורה, which has a pole at each end.

steps.title: A ספר תורה is rolled toward its middle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that other scrolls roll from start to end, but a ספר תורה rolls to the middle with a pole on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: all scrolls are rolled from their beginning to their end, but a ספר תורה is rolled to its middle, and he makes it a pole on this side and on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a ברייתא to show that a ספר תורה has a pole at each end, unlike other scrolls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a ספר תורה has two poles, each end wraps around a pole. That is why the same measure, enough to roll around the pole, fits both ends. This supports רב אשי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
on this side and on that side

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the familiar practice of a ספר תורה having two עצי חיים, one at each end.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
All scrolls are wound from their beginning to their end;
but a Torah scroll is wound to its middle,
and he makes for it a pole on this side and on that side.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא כׇּל הַסְּפָרִים נִגְלָלִים מִתְּחִלָּתָן לְסוֹפָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a ספר תורה needs the same measure at both ends.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that a ספר תורה has a pole at each end and is rolled toward the middle.

steps.title: The scribes of ירושלים did it this way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק reports that the scribes of ירושלים made their scrolls this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק said: this is how the scroll-writers in ירושלים made their scrolls.
steps.whatsHappening: An eyewitness report confirms that a scroll with a pole at each end was the actual practice in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק adds testimony about real practice: the scribes of ירושלים made scrolls with a pole on each side. This backs up the ברייתא, and with it רב אשי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנא who testifies about practice in ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רב נחמן בר יצחק says each end gets its own measure. רב אשי says the single measure is for a ספר תורה, which has a pole at each end, as the scribes of ירושלים did.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ הָיוּ כּוֹתְבֵי סְפָרִים שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם עוֹשִׂין סִפְרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: This is how the scribes in Jerusalem would make their scrolls.
phrases.notes: 'This is how' means with a pole on each side, rolled toward the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק כָּךְ הָיוּ כּוֹתְבֵי סְפָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an eyewitness report supporting the ברייתא of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a scroll with a pole at each end was the real practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Testimony of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק about the scribes of ירושלים.

steps.title: A Torah scroll's height should equal its circumference
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a ספר תורה should be made so that its height and its rolled-up circumference are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A ספר תורה should not be made taller than it is around, and it should not be thicker around than it is tall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about the right shape of a ספר תורה. The height and the circumference of the rolled scroll should match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of how scrolls are made, which came up with the poles in the earlier steps. The rule sets a target shape: the height of the parchment should equal the distance around the rolled-up scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Its length; here it means the height of the parchment
Its circumference; the distance around the scroll when it is rolled

steps.whyThisMatters: This ideal shape is the background for everything that follows: רבי's measurement, the stories about scribes, and the challenge from the ארון.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One does not make a Torah scroll
neither with its length greater than its circumference,
phrases.notes: "Length" is how tall the parchment stands; "circumference" is the distance around the rolled-up scroll.

phrases.english: nor with its circumference greater than its length.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין עוֹשִׂין סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how scrolls are rolled with poles to the proper proportions of a ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספר תורה's height should equal its rolled-up circumference.

steps.title: They ask רבי how tall a Torah scroll should be
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי what the actual size of a ספר תורה should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי: How big should a ספר תורה be?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gave a ratio but no actual number, so the students ask רבי for a real measurement. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that height equals circumference is not enough to build a scroll. You need a starting number, so they ask for the height.

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi:
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The size of a Torah scroll is how much?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete number behind the ratio in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual height of a ספר תורה.

steps.title: Six טפחים on גויל, unknown on קלף
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that a scroll on גויל is six טפחים, but he does not know the size for a scroll on קלף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: On גויל, six. They asked: On קלף, how much? He said: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a number for one kind of parchment, גויל. When asked about the other kind, קלף, he admits he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two materials have different thicknesses, so the same amount of text rolls up to a different circumference. That means the right height changes with the material. רבי knows the answer only for גויל.

keyTerms.meaning: A thick, full hide treated for writing

steps.confusionAlert: Six is a height in טפחים (handbreadths), not a count of anything else. With thinner קלף the scroll rolls up smaller, so the matching height would be different.

phrases.english: He said to them:
On gevil, six.
phrases.notes: Six טפחים (handbreadths) tall.

phrases.english: On kelaf, how much?
I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: בִּגְוִיל – שִׁשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11. A follow-up question about קלף follows, and רבי answers that he does not know.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On גויל the scroll is six טפחים tall. For קלף, רבי does not know.

steps.title: רב הונא got it right only once in seventy
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא wrote seventy ספרי תורה, and only one came out with exactly matching height and circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא wrote seventy ספרי תורה, and it worked out for him only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show how hard it is to make the height and circumference match exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an expert scribe who wrote seventy scrolls hit the perfect proportion only one time. This shows that the rule in step 10 is an ideal that is very hard to reach.

keyTerms.meaning: It happened for him, it worked out for him

phrases.english: Rav Huna wrote
seventy Torah scrolls,
and it worked out for him only with one.
phrases.notes: "Worked out" means the height and the circumference came out exactly equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא כְּתַב שִׁבְעִין סִפְרֵי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates how hard it is to achieve the proportion taught in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Getting a perfectly proportioned ספר תורה is extremely rare.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב succeeds on his first try
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב wrote one scroll on calf hide and it came out perfect. The Rabbis looked at him enviously, and he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב wrote one scroll on calf hide, and it worked out for him. The Rabbis set their eyes on him, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story: one scribe got the perfect proportion on his very first scroll. The other Rabbis gazed at him in amazement or envy, and he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of רב הונא: one try and immediate success. His achievement was so remarkable that the Rabbis' gaze, an עין הרע, is described as causing his death.

keyTerms.meaning: They set their eyes on him; an envious gaze

steps.whatToRemember: The two stories together show that the perfect proportion of a ספר תורה is an ideal that very few scribes ever reach.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב כְּתַב חַד
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov wrote one
on the hide of calves,
and it worked out for him.
The Rabbis set their eyes on him,
phrases.notes: An envious gaze, what we call an עין הרע.

phrases.english: and he passed away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב כְּתַב חַד אַמַּשְׁכֵּיהּ דְּעִיגְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting story to רב הונא's: success on the first attempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An immediate perfect scroll was so rare that it drew a deadly envious gaze.

steps.title: Report that רבי אמי wrote four hundred Torah scrolls
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis tell רב המנונא that רבי אמי wrote four hundred ספרי תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to רב המנונא: רבי אמי wrote four hundred ספרי תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the theme of writing scrolls, the Rabbis report an amazing number. This sets up רב המנונא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four hundred full ספרי תורה is a huge number for one person to write in a lifetime. The claim is brought so that it can be questioned.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Hamnuna:
Rabbi Ami wrote
four hundred Torah scrolls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another report about scroll-writing, this time a surprising number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A report that רבי אמי wrote 400 ספרי תורה.

steps.title: Perhaps he wrote only one verse four hundred times
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא suggests that רבי אמי really wrote the פסוק 'תורה צוה לנו משה' four hundred times, not four hundred whole scrolls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Perhaps he wrote 'תורה צוה לנו משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא pushes back on the report. He suggests it means רבי אמי wrote one short פסוק that begins with the word 'תורה', not entire ספרי תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא finds 400 complete ספרי תורה hard to believe for one person. So he suggests that 'writing תורה' may mean writing this short פסוק, which begins with the word 'תורה', many times over.

keyTerms.meaning: 'משה commanded us the Torah', the opening of a פסוק

phrases.english: He said to them:
Perhaps he wrote "Moses commanded us the Torah."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:4

steps.triggerLanguage: דִילְמָא ״תּוֹרָה צִוָּה לָנוּ מֹשֶׁה״ כְּתַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the report of step 15 to make it believable.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the literal reading of '400 ספרי תורה'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Writing 400 complete scrolls is not realistic. 'תורה' may refer to a single פסוק.

steps.title: Report that רבי ינאי planted four hundred vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רבי זירא that רבי ינאי planted four hundred vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבי זירא: רבי ינאי planted four hundred vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar-sounding report with the same number, four hundred. This sets up a matching explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the report about רבי אמי, this one seems too big to be literal. It is placed here because it follows the same pattern.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rabbi Zeira:
Rabbi Yannai planted
four hundred vineyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel report with the same number, 400.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A report that רבי ינאי planted 400 vineyards.

steps.title: Perhaps they were the smallest possible vineyards
steps.stepSummary: The answer: perhaps each 'vineyard' was the smallest kind the הלכה recognizes, two vines facing two with a fifth sticking out like a tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps two facing two, and one sticking out as a tail.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as in step 16, the big number is explained away. Each 'vineyard' may have been only five vines, the smallest group that counts as a vineyard in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'vineyard' does not have to mean a large field. The minimum כרם in הלכה is five vines arranged this way, so 400 of those is believable.
steps.whatToRemember: Both reports of 400 are read in a smaller way: a single פסוק instead of whole scrolls, and tiny five-vine vineyards instead of large fields.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is most likely רבי זירא answering, just as רב המנונא answered in the previous story.

phrases.english: Perhaps two opposite two,
and one sticking out as a tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא שְׁתַּיִם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁתַּיִם, וְאַחַת יוֹצֵא זָנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the report of step 17 in the same way that step 16 reinterpreted step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the literal reading of '400 vineyards' as large fields.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Vineyard' can mean the minimum five-vine כרם.

steps.title: A challenge begins from the size of משה's Ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge (מיתיבי) using the measurements of the ארון that משה made: 2.5 by 1.5 by 1.5 אמות, with each אמה being six טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The ארון that משה made was two and a half אמות long, one and a half אמות wide, and one and a half אמות high, using an אמה of six טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the size of a ספר תורה and starts a challenge by quoting the measurements of the ארון. This step only sets up the data. The ברייתא's calculations continue in steps 20–28, and the challenge itself is spelled out on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the ארון's size in אמות and says each אמה is six טפחים. In טפחים, that makes the ארון 15 long, 9 wide and 9 high. These numbers will be compared against the six-טפח scroll from רבי's answer in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged; an objection from a ברייתא
The Ark that held the לוחות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the question yet. Here the גמרא only lists the ארון's measurements. The calculations follow in the next steps, and the problem they create is spelled out on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: They challenged:
The Ark that Moses made —
phrases.notes: שמות 25:10

phrases.english: two and a half cubits was its length,
and a cubit and a half its width,
and a cubit and a half its height,
using a cubit of six handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָרוֹן שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the measurements of a ספר תורה by bringing a challenging ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a ספר תורה on גויל is six טפחים tall, with height equal to circumference.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ארון's dimensions (15 x 9 x 9 טפחים) will be used to test whether such a scroll could fit alongside what the ארון held. The calculation follows in steps 20–24.

steps.title: The size of the לוחות and the space left along the length of the ארון
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the ברייתא: the לוחות are 6 by 6 by 3 טפחים and lie side by side along the ארון's length. That uses 12 of the 15 טפחים. One טפח goes to the walls, and the remaining two טפחים hold the ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לוחות were six טפחים long, six wide and three thick, and they lay along the length of the ארון. How much of the ארון's length did they take up? Twelve טפחים. Three טפחים were left. Take one away, half for each wall, and two טפחים remain, where the ספר תורה lay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from its challenge, now giving the size of the לוחות. It works out how much of the ארון's length they fill and what was left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a six-טפח אמה, the ארון is 2.5 × 6 = 15 טפחים long. Two לוחות lying side by side, each 6 long, use 12, which leaves 3. Half a טפח for each wall's thickness leaves exactly 2 טפחים, and that space is given to the ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The two stone tablets of the עשרת הדברות
A wall, here the wooden side of the ארון

steps.confusionAlert: Don't forget the walls. The ברייתא counts the ארון's measurements from the outside, so it subtracts the thickness of the wooden sides before deciding how much empty space is really left inside.

phrases.english: And the tablets: their length was six
their width six, and their thickness three;
phrases.notes: All these numbers are in טפחים, handbreadths.

phrases.english: they were placed along the length of the Ark.
How much do the tablets take up in the Ark?
Twelve handbreadths.
Three handbreadths were left there.
Take away one handbreadth from them:

phrases.aramaic: חֶצְיוֹ לְכוֹתֶל זֶה וְחֶצְיוֹ לְכוֹתֶל זֶה –
phrases.english: half for this wall and half for that wall.
Two handbreadths were left there,
in which the Torah scroll lay.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַלּוּחוֹת – אׇרְכָּן שִׁשָּׁה, וְרׇחְבָּן שִׁשָּׁה, וְעׇבְיָין שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 19, adding the size of the לוחות to the ארון's measurements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Along the ארון's length, after the לוחות (12) and the walls (1), two טפחים remain for the ספר תורה.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that a ספר תורה was in the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves a ספר תורה lay in the ארון from 'אין בארון רק,' which contains two limiting words. Two limitations in a row come to include something, and here that something is the ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'There was nothing in the Ark except the two stone tablets that משה placed there.' What does 'nothing in the Ark except' teach? It is a limitation after a limitation, and a limitation after a limitation always comes to include something more: the Torah scroll lying in the Ark.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to back up its claim that a ספר תורה sat in the leftover space of the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'אין' (nothing) and 'רק' (only) are words that limit. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, two limiting words in a row actually widen the meaning. So the פסוק hints that something besides the לוחות was there: the ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A limitation after a limitation, which comes to include rather than exclude

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but 'nothing except' is read here as a hint that something more was inside, not as proof that the ארון held only the לוחות.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'There was nothing in the Ark except'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:9

phrases.english: the two tablets of stone
which Moses placed there [etc.]'
phrases.notes: The square-bracket 'וגו׳' just means the פסוק keeps going.

phrases.english: What does 'nothing in the Ark except' teach?
It is a limitation after a limitation;
phrases.notes: 'אין' is one limiting word and 'רק' is the second.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת –
phrases.english: and a limitation after a limitation only comes to include:
the Torah scroll that lay in the Ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֵין בָּאָרוֹן רַק שְׁנֵי לֻחוֹת הָאֲבָנִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 20's claim that a ספר תורה lay in the ארון.
steps.raayaObject: That a ספר תורה was placed in the ארון next to the לוחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 8:9, 'אין בארון רק,' read as מיעוט אחר מיעוט.

steps.title: The space left across the width of the ארון
steps.stepSummary: Across the ארון's 9-טפח width, the לוחות take up 6. After one טפח for the walls, two טפחים remain, so the ספר תורה can go in and out without being squeezed. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have accounted for the ארון's length; now account for its width. How much of the width do the לוחות take up? Six טפחים. Three are left. Take away one, half for each wall, and two remain, so the ספר תורה will not be squeezed going in and out. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Having worked out the length, the ברייתא now does the same math for the width of the ארון. It then tells us that this whole calculation is רבי מאיר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The width is 1.5 × 6 = 9 טפחים. The לוחות, each 6 wide, fill 6, leaving 3. After one טפח for the walls, 2 remain. That extra room gives the ספר תורה space to slide in and out freely.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'you have provided for,' meaning you have accounted for all the space

phrases.english: You have accounted for the Ark along its length;
go and account for the Ark along its width:
How much do the tablets take up in the Ark?
Six handbreadths.
Three handbreadths were left there;
take away one handbreadth from them:

phrases.aramaic: חֶצְיוֹ לְכוֹתֶל זֶה וְחֶצְיוֹ לְכוֹתֶל זֶה –
phrases.english: half for this wall and half for that wall.
Two handbreadths were left there,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה נִכְנָס וְיוֹצֵא
phrases.english: so that the Torah scroll would not go in and out
while being squeezed;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר (six-טפח אמה), the ארון had two free טפחים along its length for the ספר תורה and two free טפחים across its width so the scroll would not be squeezed.
steps.triggerLanguage: פִּירְנַסְתָּ אָרוֹן לְאׇרְכּוֹ; צֵא וּפַרְנֵס אָרוֹן לְרׇחְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the length (step 20) to the width of the ארון, and names רבי מאיר as the author of the calculation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Across the width, two טפחים remain so the ספר תורה is not squeezed going in and out (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds the אמה is five טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה measures the ארון with a five-טפח אמה, making it 12.5 טפחים long. The לוחות still take up 12, leaving only half a טפח, which is used up by one fingerbreadth for each wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the measurements use an אמה of five טפחים. The לוחות were six long, six wide and three thick, lying along the length of the ארון. How much did they take up? Twelve טפחים. Half a טפח was left: one fingerbreadth for this wall and one fingerbreadth for that wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings רבי יהודה, who disagrees with רבי מאיר about the size of the אמה. He redoes the length calculation with the smaller number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a five-טפח אמה, the ארון is 2.5 × 5 = 12.5 טפחים long. The לוחות still fill 12, so only half a טפח (two fingerbreadths) remains, and the two walls use all of it. In רבי יהודה's view, there is no room along the length for a ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit of five handbreadths, a smaller אמה than רבי מאיר's
A fingerbreadth; four make one טפח

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement over the size of the אמה changes whether there is any room for a ספר תורה along the ארון's length. This shapes how the גמרא will use the ברייתא in its challenge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With a cubit of five handbreadths.
And the tablets: their length was six,
their width six, and their thickness three;
they were placed along the length of the Ark.
How much do the tablets take up in the Ark?
Twelve handbreadths;
half a handbreadth was left there:

phrases.aramaic: אֶצְבַּע לְכוֹתֶל זֶה וְאֶצְבַּע לְכוֹתֶל זֶה.
phrases.english: one fingerbreadth for this wall and one fingerbreadth for that wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּאַמָּה בַּת חֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's view against רבי מאיר's calculation in steps 20–22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a five-טפח אמה, only half a טפח remains along the length, and the two walls use it all up.

steps.title: Measuring the ארון's width in רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The ארון is 7.5 טפחים wide. The לוחות take up 6, the walls take up half a טפח, and the last טפח holds the pillars.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have accounted for the ארון's length. Now account for its width. How much space do the לוחות take? Six טפחים. One and a half טפחים are left. Subtract half a טפח for the two walls, a fingerbreadth and a half for each one. One טפח is left, and that is where the pillars stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now does the width math for רבי יהודה, just as it did the length math in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a five-טפח אמה, 1.5 אמות is 7.5 טפחים. The לוחות are 6 טפחים wide, so 1.5 טפחים remain. After the walls, the one טפח left over holds pillars, not a ספר תורה. This is different from רבי מאיר, who had two טפחים free for the ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Account for, or fill in, the space
Fingerbreadth, a small unit smaller than a טפח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. For רבי מאיר the extra space held the ספר תורה. For רבי יהודה the space is filled by walls and pillars, so there is no room for a ספר תורה inside.

phrases.english: You have accounted for the Ark's length;
go and account for the Ark's width.
How much space do the tablets take up in the Ark?
phrases.notes: With רבי יהודה's five-טפח אמה, the ארון's width of 1.5 אמות comes to 7.5 טפחים.

phrases.english: Six handbreadths.
One and a half handbreadths were left there;
take away half a handbreadth from them:
one and a half fingerbreadths for this wall
and one and a half fingerbreadths for that wall.
One handbreadth was left there,
in which the pillars stood,

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּירְנַסְתָּ אָרוֹן לְאׇרְכּוֹ; צֵא וּפַרְנֵס אָרוֹן לְרׇחְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's length calculation to his width calculation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's view the ארון's width is filled by the לוחות (6), the walls (half a טפח), and the pillars (1 טפח).

steps.title: A פסוק that mentions the pillars
steps.stepSummary: The pillars in the ארון are supported by the פסוק about שלמה's canopy, which says 'its pillars he made of silver.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'King שלמה made himself a canopy of the wood of Lebanon. He made its pillars of silver, its covering of gold, its seat of purple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to show that the ארון really had pillars that took up that last טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The canopy in שיר השירים is read as a hint to the ארון. The words 'its pillars he made of silver' show that the ארון had silver pillars, which explains the leftover טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Canopy or palanquin, read here as a hint to the ארון

phrases.english: as it is said: "King Solomon made himself a canopy
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 3:9–10

phrases.english: of the wood of Lebanon;
its pillars he made of silver,
its covering of gold, its seat of purple, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַפִּרְיוֹן עָשָׂה לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the pillars mentioned in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: That pillars stood inside the ארון

steps.title: The פלשתים' chest stood beside the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The chest that the פלשתים sent with their gift was placed next to the ארון, as the פסוק in שמואל says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The chest in which the פלשתים sent a gift to the God of Israel was placed beside the ארון, as it says: 'And the golden objects that you are returning to Him as a guilt offering, put in the chest at its side, and send it off, and it will go.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since there is no room inside the ארון for a ספר תורה in רבי יהודה's view, the ברייתא now describes what stood next to the ארון. This sets up where the ספר תורה was kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פלשתים returned the ארון with golden gifts in a chest, and the פסוק says the chest went 'at its side.' The ברייתא learns that this chest stayed beside the ארון.

phrases.english: And the chest in which the Philistines sent
a gift to the God of Israel
was placed at its side,
as it is said: "And the golden objects
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:8

phrases.english: that you are returning to Him as a guilt offering,
put in the chest at its side,
and send it off, and it will go."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְגַּז שֶׁשִּׁיגְּרוּ בּוֹ פְּלִשְׁתִּים דּוֹרוֹן לֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּנָּח מִצִּדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After filling the inside of the ארון, the ברייתא turns to what stood outside, beside it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פלשתים' chest was placed beside the ארון.

steps.title: The ספר תורה lay on the chest, beside the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The ספר תורה rested on top of that chest. The פסוק says to put it 'at the side of the ארון,' meaning next to it and not inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on the chest the ספר תורה was placed, as it says: 'Take this ספר תורה and place it at the side of the ארון of the covenant of ה׳.' It was placed at the side, not inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us where the ספר תורה was kept according to רבי יהודה: on the chest next to the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the ספר תורה lay inside the ארון. רבי יהודה reads the word 'מצד' in דברים literally: next to the ארון, not in it. This fits his math, which left no room inside.

keyTerms.meaning: At the side of, next to

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the ספר תורה was inside the ארון. רבי יהודה: the ספר תורה lay on the פלשתים' chest beside the ארון.

phrases.english: And on it a Torah scroll was placed,
phrases.notes: 'On it' means on the פלשתים' chest from the previous line.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Take this Torah scroll,
phrases.notes: דברים 31:26

phrases.aramaic: וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֹתוֹ מִצַּד אֲרוֹן בְּרִית ה׳״ –
phrases.english: and place it at the side of the Ark of the covenant of ה׳"
at the side it was placed,
and not inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעָלָיו סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מוּנָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the chest from the previous step as the place where the ספר תורה rested.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the ספר תורה was beside the ארון on the chest, not inside it.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה explain 'אין בארון רק'?
steps.stepSummary: If the ספר תורה was not inside the ארון, what do the two limiting words in 'אין בארון רק' come to include? The answer begins: 'to include...'
steps.simpleTranslation: So how do I explain the פסוק 'There is nothing in the ארון except'? It comes to include...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how רבי יהודה deals with the פסוק that רבי מאיר used to put the ספר תורה inside the ארון, and it starts to answer. The answer finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, two limiting words in a row ('אין' and 'רק') were read as including the ספר תורה inside the ארון. רבי יהודה has just placed the ספר תורה outside, so the extra inclusion must point to something else. The word 'לרבות' tells us he still agrees the פסוק includes something.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain or fulfill (this פסוק)?

phrases.english: And how do I explain
"There is nothing in the Ark except"?
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:9, the same פסוק from step 21, read there as including the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: It comes to include...

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״אֵין בָּאָרוֹן רַק״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having placed the ספר תורה outside the ארון, the ברייתא must explain רבי מאיר's source verse in a new way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the double limitation in 'אין בארון רק' includes, if not the ספר תורה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It comes 'to include' something else. The rest of the answer continues on the next עמוד.
